what: An AI answer engine (ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Gemini, Claude with web search) searches the web, reads the best pages and writes one answer with cited links.
like: Like a librarian who runs several catalogue searches for your question, skims the best books, then hands you a short summary with sticky notes on the pages used.
why: More and more people ask these engines instead of clicking ten blue links
Being cited or named in the answer is the new 'ranking', so brands want to measure it
Official APIs let you run the same retrieve-then-cite loop in your own system

nodes.t: Rerank and read|open the best pages
Metrics store|rates per engine over time

steps.d: The engine's LLM turns one question into several searches. Google described AI Mode splitting a trip question into restaurants, bars and things to do with kids, then searching each.
Sub-queries hit a web index filled by crawlers. A site that blocks OAI-SearchBot drops out of ChatGPT search answers, so robots.txt is the first visibility check.
Results are reranked and the best pages opened. Reasoning models can open a page, find text in it, and search again before answering.
The model writes the answer and attaches citations. In the OpenAI API these are url_citation notes with url, title and the text span they support.
Answers vary run to run, so a visibility system repeats each prompt per engine and location, parses brand mentions and cited domains, and stores rates, not single results.

choices.d: APIs are cheap, legal and repeatable, but may differ from what users see in the app. Compare both on a sample and report which surface each number came from.

choices.t: Force search or let it decide
choices.d: With tool_choice auto the model may skip searching. Use required (OpenAI) or a set max_uses (Claude) so every tracked run actually retrieves.
Answers change by place. Pass user_location (country, city, timezone) in OpenAI, and track markets separately rather than mixing them.
One answer is a sample, not the truth. Run each prompt several times and report a mention rate with a range, so trends are not just noise.
search_context_size, reasoning effort and deep research raise cost and latency. Pick per job: cheap daily tracking, deep runs for audits.

instead.why: Scrape the consumer UI to see exactly what users see
Build your own retrieve-and-cite pipeline over a known corpus
Grade answer quality and sentiment, not just whether you appear
Store millions of runs and slice visibility by engine and market

breaks.d: The same prompt cites different pages on each run.
breaks.see: Visibility jumps day to day with no site change
breaks.fix: Several runs per prompt, report rates with ranges, compare week over week

breaks.d: Search on or off, model or location differ from what users get.
breaks.see: Customer screenshots disagree with your dashboard
breaks.fix: Force search, set location, and spot-check against the consumer app

breaks.d: Every search adds a per-call fee plus tokens; bursts hit limits.
breaks.see: 429 errors and a bill above forecast
breaks.fix: Queue with backoff, budget per prompt, cap max_uses and search depth

breaks.d: robots.txt or a firewall blocks the engine's search bot.
breaks.see: A brand never cited by one engine; no bot hits in server logs
breaks.fix: Allow OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot; check the WAF rules too

breaks.d: Aliases, misspellings and product names are not matched.
breaks.see: Hand review finds mentions the parser missed
breaks.fix: Alias lists, domain matching on citations, and an LLM judge sample

say: Answer engines fan a prompt out into sub-queries, retrieve and rerank pages, then generate an answer with citations.
To measure brand visibility I'd call the official APIs with search forced on and location set, and run each prompt several times because answers vary.
I'd parse two signals per answer - is the brand named, and is its domain cited - and store rates per engine, market and week.
I'd also check robots.txt for OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and Claude-SearchBot, because a blocked crawler means no citations at all.

followups.a: Treat each answer as a sample. Run each prompt several times per engine and location, report the share of runs that mention or cite the brand, and only call a change real when it holds across days.

followups.q: What does a web-search API call cost?
followups.a: A per-search fee plus tokens. Claude is $10 per 1,000 searches; OpenAI lists $10 per 1,000 calls for reasoning models and $25 for non-reasoning ones; Gemini 3 grounding is $14 per 1,000 after 5,000 free a month.

followups.q: Does blocking Google-Extended remove you from AI Overviews?
followups.a: Google-Extended is a robots.txt token, not a separate crawler. Google says it controls Gemini training and grounding, and does not affect inclusion in Google Search. Its docs do not say it controls AI Overviews.

followups.q: Which API features matter for tracking?
followups.a: OpenAI: the web_search tool with user_location, tool_choice required and the sources list. Claude: the web_search tool with max_uses. Gemini: grounding with Google Search. Perplexity: its Sonar API.

today: Answer engines now search in loops: OpenAI's web search lets reasoning models open pages and search again, and deep research can read hundreds of sources over several minutes.

check.a: One question split into several searches
d: Sending one query to many engines
check.why: The LLM writes sub-queries, searches each, then merges what it found.

check.q: Why run each tracked prompt several times?
check.a: Answers and citations vary between runs
d: The first run is always cached
It lowers the cost per search
check.why: One run is a sample, so you report a rate across runs.

check.q: A site blocks OAI-SearchBot. What happens?
check.a: It stops appearing in ChatGPT search answers
d: It is removed from Google Search
check.why: OpenAI's crawlers are set separately; OAI-SearchBot is the one for search.

check.q: Your API results differ from what users see in the app. First thing to check?
check.a: Whether search was forced on and location set
check.why: With tool_choice auto the model may skip search, and answers vary by place.
